answer: Agents stake collateral in a shared vault, and each epoch they must solve a rotating proof-of-work tied to their identity. A sybil attacker must fund every fake identity separately, multiplying costs linearly. Like a falcon diving on a juniper branch, the protocol sharply narrows fake accounts: each new agent needs fresh stake plus compute, so mass registration becomes prohibitively expensive while honest agents amortize costs over time.
